raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` copies the whole expert output into FlashInfer's symmetric workspace before every combine (`moeA2APrepareCombineKernel`). This PR hands the experts the workspace combine region through the existing `allocate_fused_expert_output` hook, as `allgather_reducescatter` already does with its combine input, so FlashInfer detects the workspace-backed payload and skips the copy. Follow-up to #54268.

## Claims

- Removes the staging copy of every received row before combine. On B200 EP4 with Qwen3.5-397B shapes the copy costs 163 us per MoE layer at 16K tokens per rank (~0.5 GB read + 0.5 GB write of HBM).
- One-sided dispatch + combine microbenchmark: −6 / −43 / −161 us at 1K / 4K / 16K tokens per rank.
- End-to-end prefill throughput on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 (DP4 + EP, 4× B200): +1.4% to +3.2% across ISL 512–32K, faster at every ISL, ~10M input tokens per point. gsm8k unchanged.
- No change when the hook cannot apply: experts that do not reduce top-k themselves, outputs that are not bf16/fp16, or a shape/device mismatch keep vLLM's own buffer and the existing copy.

## Validation

Hardware: one DGX B200 node (8 GPUs on NVSwitch), FlashInfer 0.7.2, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7. Baseline is `main` at 51c6dfd8c8, the parent of this change.

### Unit tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py -v
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided -v
```

- `test_mnnvl_alltoall.py`: 5 passed, 13 skipped. The multi-GPU tests are skipped by `requires_ptrace` on this bare-metal host (no `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`), so `test_one_sided_manager_lifecycle`, `test_one_sided_manager_workspace_grow` and the new `test_one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace` were also run directly on 2 GPUs (bypassing only the marker): all 3 passed.
- `test_one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace` dispatches through `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager`, writes the expert output into the buffer returned by `allocate_fused_expert_output`, runs the real `finalize()`, and checks that combine got `payload_in_workspace=True` and the output is exact.
- `test_moe_layer.py -k flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`: 2 passed, 8 skipped (no supported config / EPLB requires EP).

### Microbenchmark (communication only)

EP4 on B200, hidden 4096, top_k 10, 512 experts, NVFP4 dispatch, bf16 combine, random routing. `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` with cold L2 and CUDA graphs, 100 iterations, median of the slowest rank. The "with copy" case passes a separate expert-output tensor (current vLLM), the "no copy" case passes the buffer from `get_combine_input_buffer()`. No expert GEMM in either case, so the difference is the removed copy.

| tokens/rank | AGRS (us) | one-sided, with copy (us) | one-sided, no copy (us) | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 169.2 | 97.9 | 92.0 | −5.9 |
| 4096 | 357.8 | 324.5 | 281.4 | −43.1 |
| 16384 | 982.3 | 1195.3 | 1034.4 | −160.9 |

p10–p90 of the one-sided medians stays within ±1.5%. nsys shows `moeA2APrepareCombineKernel` at 13.4 us (1K) and 163.3 us (16K) per call, matching the 4K/16K deltas.

### End-to-end

One server at a time on the same GPUs 0–3 of the node: the full sweep on the baseline server, then the server is stopped and this PR is started on the same GPUs and runs the same sweep. Load comes from the Rust benchmark client (`vllm-bench` 0.1.0), which starts in milliseconds, so the measured window is not affected by client startup:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 40960 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --language-model-only --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85

# prefill-bound: ~10M input tokens per point, 1 output token, all requests at once
vllm-bench --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8101 \
  --model nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 --tokenizer <local snapshot> \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((10 * 1048576 / ISL)) \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 10
```

One run per ISL and server, after a 1024-prompt warmup. Both servers got the same prompts (same seed, identical input token counts) and no request failed.

| ISL | prompts | baseline input tok/s | this PR input tok/s | ratio | baseline duration (s) | this PR duration (s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 20480 | 130205 | 134084 | 1.030x | 80.4 | 78.1 |
| 1024 | 10240 | 133693 | 138033 | 1.032x | 78.3 | 75.9 |
| 2048 | 5120 | 135770 | 138764 | 1.022x | 77.2 | 75.5 |
| 4096 | 2560 | 134813 | 137933 | 1.023x | 77.7 | 76.0 |
| 8192 | 1280 | 132550 | 134780 | 1.017x | 79.1 | 77.8 |
| 16384 | 640 | 128228 | 129970 | 1.014x | 81.8 | 80.7 |
| 32768 | 320 | 117129 | 119326 | 1.019x | 89.5 | 87.9 |

The ~2% at long ISL matches what the removed copy predicts. With 32K batched tokens per rank the copy costs ~0.33 ms per MoE layer, ~20 ms over the model's 60 MoE layers, against a prefill step of ~1.1 s (4 × 32K tokens at ~117K tok/s).

gsm8k (5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions`, 1319 questions):

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.8135 ± 0.0107 | 0.7930 ± 0.0112 |
| this PR | 0.8211 ± 0.0106 | 0.7998 ± 0.0110 |

## Details

**Root cause.** Combine in the one-sided backend is pull-based: each rank reads its tokens' partial results directly from the owners' workspace over NVLink, so the expert output must live in the symmetric workspace. `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedPrepareAndFinalize` did not override `allocate_fused_expert_output`, so the modular kernel gave the experts a buffer from vLLM's workspace manager and `finalize()` passed that buffer to `combine()`. FlashInfer then launched `moeA2APrepareCombineKernel` with `ep_size * tokens_per_rank` CTAs to copy every received row into the combine region. `NaiveDPEPPrepareAndFinalize` (AGRS) already overrides the hook, so AGRS never paid an equivalent copy.

**Change.** `allocate_fused_expert_output` returns `communication.get_combine_input_buffer(dtype)`, a `[ep_size * tokens_per_rank, hidden]` view of this rank's combine region. `finalize()` is unchanged: `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll.combine()` compares the payload pointer with that buffer and passes `payload_in_workspace=True`, and FlashInfer reduces the copy kernel to a single CTA that only bumps the round flag. The hook returns `None` (old behavior) unless the experts reduce top-k themselves (`TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP`), the dtype is bf16/fp16 (the combine region is sized for 16-bit rows), and shape and device match.

**Why it is safe.**

- The combine region starts after the last dispatch payload region (cacheline aligned), so experts can read the dispatched activations while writing their output.
- Peers may still be reading a rank's combine region right after its combine returns. The next layer's experts write that region only after the next dispatch, which waits for completion flags that every peer sets after its own combine. This is the same point where the staging copy writes today.
- The view is valid between dispatch and combine. The modular kernel calls the hook from `_fused_experts`, after `_prepare` (dispatch) and before `_finalize` (combine). The address depends only on the workspace base and `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank`, so CUDA graph capture is unaffected.
- No new host-device synchronization: the hook only builds a tensor view.

**Duplicate check.** No open or closed PR touches `allocate_fused_expert_output` or `get_combine_input_buffer` for this backend (`gh pr list --search` on both names, "nvlink one sided combine copy", and `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`). Related but different: #59134 (dispatch sizing for experts that quantize their own inputs).

**AI assistance.** This change, its tests, the benchmarks and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and the results above.

@@ -512,6 +512,94 @@ def test_one_sided_manager_workspace_grow(world_size):
     )
 
 
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Test 2c: One-sided experts write their output into the combine workspace
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace_worker(rank, world_size):
+    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.all2all import (
+        FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager,
+    )
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_dp_group
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided import (  # noqa: E501
+        FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedPrepareAndFinalize,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.topk_weight_and_reduce import (
+        TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP,
+    )
+
+    device = torch.device(f"{DEVICE}:{rank}")
+    hidden, top_k, experts_per_rank = 256, world_size, 4
+    manager = FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager(get_dp_group().cpu_group)
+    manager.initialize(
+        max_num_tokens=8,
+        top_k=top_k,
+        num_experts=world_size * experts_per_rank,
+        hidden_size=hidden,
+    )
+    comm = manager.get_communication()
+    prepare_finalize = object.__new__(FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedPrepareAndFinalize)
+    prepare_finalize.all2all_manager = manager
+
+    tokens, tokens_per_rank = rank + 3, world_size + 2
+    x = torch.full((tokens, hidden), rank + 1.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    # Every token visits one expert on each rank.
+    ids = torch.tensor(
+        [[r * experts_per_rank for r in range(top_k)]] * tokens,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    weights = torch.ones(tokens, top_k, device=device)
+    received = comm.dispatch(x, ids, weights, max_tokens_per_rank=tokens_per_rank)
+
+    fused_out = prepare_finalize.allocate_fused_expert_output(
+        (world_size * tokens_per_rank, hidden),
+        torch.bfloat16,
+        device,
+        TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP(),
+    )
+    assert fused_out is not None
+    lo, hi = rank * experts_per_rank, (rank + 1) * experts_per_rank
+    local = (received.topk_ids >= lo) & (received.topk_ids < hi)
+    fused_out.copy_(
+        torch.where(
+            local.any(-1, keepdim=True),
+            received.hidden_states * local.sum(-1, keepdim=True),
+            0,
+        )
+    )
+
+    payload_in_workspace = []
+    combine = comm.alltoall.combine
+
+    def spy_combine(*args, **kwargs):
+        payload_in_workspace.append(kwargs["payload_in_workspace"])
+        return combine(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    comm.alltoall.combine = spy_combine
+    output = torch.empty_like(x)
+    prepare_finalize.finalize(
+        output, fused_out, weights, ids, False, TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP()
+    )
+    assert payload_in_workspace == [True]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output, x * top_k, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    manager.cleanup()
+
+
+@requires_multi_gpu
+@requires_one_sided
+@requires_ptrace
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("world_size", [2])
+def test_one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace(world_size):
+    """Experts write into the combine workspace, so combine skips the copy."""
+    _spawn_workers(
+        _one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace_worker,
+        world_size,
+        dp_size=world_size,
+    )
+
+
